findings.title: Error events are repeated and misplaced across summary pages
findings.body: `analyze_recording_segments` is passed to `paginate` via `functools.partial` (line 100), so it runs once per page with only that page's segments. `GenericOffsetPaginator` calls `data_fn(offset=..., limit=...)` per page (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:524). `gen_request_data` starts `error_idx = 0` on every call (line 146) and, after the segment loop, yields every remaining error (lines 164-168). An error earlier than a page's first event is emitted at the start of that page, and every error after a page's last event is emitted at the end of that page, so the same error can appear in several pages' summary inputs. Limit errors to the page's time window, or emit each error once across the replay. Confidence is medium because I did not read the `paginate` helper that calls `on_results`.

findings.title: Error lookup runs on every page request and the nodestore read is unchunked
findings.body: `get` runs `query_replay_instance` (Snuba) and then `fetch_error_details` (nodestore) before `self.paginate` (lines 70-94), so each page request repeats the whole-replay error lookup. `fetch_error_details` passes every error ID to one `nodestore.backend.get_multi` call (line 108), with no chunking. `bulk_fetch_events` in delayed_workflow.py:453-455 chunks the same kind of call by EVENT_LIMIT. Consider caching the error list per replay or running the lookup for the first page only, and chunking the nodestore read.

findings.title: Error `id` is paired with the wrong nodestore value when a node is missing
findings.body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairs IDs with dict values by position. If `get_multi` omits missing node IDs rather than returning None for them, each later `id` is attached to the wrong event. The `id` field is not used in `generate_error_log_message` (lines 126-131), so the summary text is unaffected today. Look up each event by its node ID instead of zipping.

findings.title: Storage deletion errors are dropped silently while the replay is archived
findings.body: `pool.map(_delete_if_exists, ...)` returns a lazy iterator. Exceptions raised by the workers are only re-raised when the results are iterated, and nothing iterates here. `_delete_if_exists` only handles `NotFound` (lines 80-83), so any other storage error (timeouts, 5xx, rate limits) is lost. `delete_matched_rows` then calls `delete_replays`, which archives the replays (lines 58-61). Recording blobs can remain with no log and no error returned to the user. Collect the futures and re-raise or count failures, or iterate the results so errors surface.

findings.title: One invalid report now rejects the whole batch, including its valid reports
findings.body: Before this change the endpoint recorded a metric for every report with no per-field validation. Now the loop returns 422 on the first invalid report (lines 108-118), and metrics are emitted only after the loop (lines 122-128), so none of the batch is counted. `type` only accepts the eight listed values (lines 21-30, 40), so a report of another type, such as `network-error`, rejects the batch. `url` is a DRF `URLField` (line 41), which requires an http(s) scheme, so a document URL such as `about:blank` also rejects it. Decide whether strict rejection is intended, or record each valid report and drop only the invalid ones.

findings.title: Table widget flag branch renders empty data and ignores loading
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is on, the branch passes `columns={[]}` and an empty `tableData` (lines 165-174), so the table never shows the query results. It also skips the `loading` handling and the SPANS loading exception that the else branch keeps (lines 176-192). The flag is not registered in src/sentry/features, so this is unreachable today, but it will render blank tables once the flag is registered. Wire the branch to `result.data` and `result.meta`, or remove it until the data mapping exists.

findings.title: Unused `_handle_regex_match` left in `parametrize_w_experiments`
findings.body: After the `else` branch that used this callback was removed, `_handle_regex_match` (lines 335-343) is defined but never referenced in `parametrize_w_experiments`. Delete it. The copy in `parametrize_w_regex` (lines 310-318) is still used.

findings.title: The per-variant "Type" row is removed for every grouping variant
findings.body: The diff removes the `t('Type')` row, including its tooltip, from every switch case (COMPONENT, CUSTOM_FINGERPRINT, BUILT_IN_FINGERPRINT, SALTED_COMPONENT, PERFORMANCE_PROBLEM). The variant type is no longer shown anywhere in this table. The PR body does not mention this. Was this intentional? If not, restore the row.

findings.title: Default autofix tuning changed from "low" to "off" for every project without an explicit value
findings.body: `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` changes from "low" to "off" here, and the project option default changes too (src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:205). Existing stored settings are unaffected, but projects and orgs that never set it stop getting automatic autofix runs on new issues. The PR body does not describe this. Was the change intended and announced?

findings.title: Each merged-PR comment issue triggers a recommended-event lookup
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue listed in the comment, and that runs a Snuba query per issue. The GitHub and GitLab comment builders call it once per issue inside a list comprehension (src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:404-411). A broad except (lines 591-596) hides failures, so the comment still posts without the environment. Consider fetching environments in one batched query, or limiting how many issues get this lookup.

findings.title: Merged-PR comment drops the culprit and puts the title inside a markdown link
findings.body: The old template showed the culprit (subtitle) after the title. The new template (line 143) does not show it at all. The title now sits inside the link text `[**{title}**]`, so a title containing `]` or other markdown control characters breaks the link. Titles come from user-controlled exception messages. Confirm dropping the culprit was intended, and escape the title if it appears in link text.

findings.title: 60s processing deadline for a chunk that makes one IdP refresh per identity
findings.body: `check_auth_identities` now has a 60s deadline (lines 76-78). Each identity in a chunk of 100 calls `provider.refresh_identity` (line 128), an external request. A chunk that exceeds the deadline is killed before the reschedule at line 99, so the check chain can stall until the periodic task runs again. Confirm 60s is enough for a full chunk, or reduce `chunk_size`.

findings.title: Autofix automation default flips to 'off' for every project that never stored a value
findings.body: The default for sentry:autofix_automation_tuning changes from low to off (projectoptions/defaults.py:205; the org default constant at constants.py:724 changes the same way). ProjectOptionManager.get_value returns the registered well-known default when no row exists (models/options/project_option.py:111-114), so every existing project that never saved this option now reads off. _is_issue_fixable returns False for off (seer/issue_summary.py:253-254), so automatic autofix on new issues stops for those projects. Neither this change nor the PR description (Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System) mentions it, and no log or UI state tells users it happened. Please confirm this is intended and announce it. If it is not intended, restore low at both constants.py:724 and projectoptions/defaults.py:205. The automation runner (_run_automation) was not read, so the effect on automation is inferred from _is_issue_fixable.

findings.title: Merged-PR comment format changed beyond the culprit removal
findings.body: Both the GitHub and GitLab merged-PR comments now build each entry from the shared template in commit_context.py:143. Compared with the removed templates, the culprit subtitle no longer appears, the title becomes the link instead of a separate View Issue link, and the environment is appended. The template ends in a newline and the entries are joined with a newline, so each entry is followed by a blank line. None of this is in the PR description. Confirm that dropping the culprit from customer-visible comments is intended and that the blank-line spacing is acceptable. The test_pr_comment files in other parts assert the new output.

findings.title: format_comment_subtitle helpers are now dead code
findings.body: After this change nothing in src/ calls GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.format_comment_subtitle (line 394) or GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.format_comment_subtitle (src/sentry/integrations/gitlab/integration.py:240). The truncation they performed now lives in PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title (commit_context.py:578-582). Remove both helpers unless tests call them directly; the search only covered src/.

findings.title: Assemble analytics fires on every POST, before the feature gate, including polls
findings.body: analytics.record runs before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble check (lines 88-91) and before request validation (lines 94-96). The endpoint is polled: a POST whose chunks are not all uploaded gets NOT_FOUND (lines 117-120), and every poll now emits the event. The counter therefore measures requests, not assemblies, and includes orgs without the feature. Confirm this is the intended metric. If it should count assemblies, move the call after the feature check and the chunk and state checks. The call itself is safe: org-token callers get AnonymousUser() (api/authentication.py:518, 552), whose id is None, and user_id is required=False.

findings.title: DB query injection detections are suppressed until the fifth occurrence
findings.body: noise_config = NoiseConfig(ignore_limit=5) makes should_create_group return False for the first four occurrences of a grouphash within the 24h expiry window (grouptype.py:684-700). Before this change the type had no noise config and should_create_group returned True every time (grouptype.py:681-682). The type is released=False by default (grouptype.py:200), so this applies to flagged organizations only. It matches the other performance types (grouptype.py:354, 377), but this type is a vulnerability detector, and the PR does not say the delay is intended. Confirm it is intended.

findings.title: Attachment wrapper loses overflow hidden, so long file names may not ellipsize
findings.body: The old FlexCenter wrapper applied p.theme.overflowEllipsis (theme.tsx:477-483: overflow hidden, text-overflow ellipsis, nowrap). Flex sets none of these (core/layout/flex.tsx:18-26). The wrapper is a grid item in a 1fr auto auto track (eventAttachments.tsx:199-201). Without overflow hidden, its automatic minimum width is its min-content width, which for a long nowrap file name is the full name, so the track may widen instead of truncating. The Name child still has its own ellipsis (203-206). I did not render this. Check a long attachment name in the event attachments table, or keep the wrapper's ellipsis styling.

findings.title: New snuba-metrics mode containerized-metrics-dev is not verifiable from this repo
findings.body: The snuba-metrics service points at snuba mode containerized-metrics-dev (lines 23-29), and the new tracing profile depends on it. This repo does not define that mode, so confirm it exists in the snuba devservices config. The four new subscription-results consumers do exist: they are defined in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:299-324, mapped in src/sentry/conf/server.py:3336-3339, and listed as programs here (lines 131-139 and 325-332).

findings.title: Hidden attributes are only filtered while a search is typed
findings.body: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (line 34) is applied only inside the search branch. When the search box is empty, the early return at lines 61-63 returns `sorted` unfiltered, so `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are listed. Typing any query filters them out, so the list changes with and without a search. Apply the `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` check before the search branch so both paths hide them.

findings.title: Header row lost its vertical centering and gap in the refactor
findings.body: The removed `FlexBox`/`Container` styles were `display:flex; align-items:center; gap: space(1)`, with `justify-content: space-between` added on the container. The new `<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">` at line 93 sets no `align` or `gap`, so `align-items` falls back to stretch and the tabs and vitals have no gap between them. The second placeholder group (line 27) lost the same two properties. Pass `align="center"` and `gap={space(1)}` to match the previous layout.

findings.title: Attribute-key request no longer opts out of retries
findings.body: The removed `useApiQuery` call passed `retry: false`. The `useQuery` call at lines 50-54 does not, and the app's client config (static/app/utils/queryClient.tsx:19-26) sets no retry override. A failing `/trace-items/attributes/` request is therefore retried with react-query's default backoff before `error` is set, and `isLoading` (line 61) stays true for that whole window. The explore search bar and span tag context show loading throughout. Restore `retry: false`. The default retry count comes from the react-query version, which I did not read in the repository.

findings.title: `isLoading` now reports every background refetch, not only the first load
findings.body: `isLoading` is now `isFetching` (line 61). The removed code used `result.isLoading`, which is true only with no cached data. With the default staleTime of 0, every mount refetches, so `numberAttributesLoading` and `stringAttributesLoading` (static/app/views/explore/contexts/traceItemAttributeContext.tsx:43-57) flip to true while cached keys are still shown. That flag reaches `useTraceItemAttributes().isLoading` (traceItemAttributeContext.tsx:98-117), which static/app/views/explore/contexts/spanTagsContext.tsx:4 reads. Keep the no-data meaning for the flag, for example by returning `isPending`, if the old behavior is wanted.

findings.title: Attribute-key request drops the environment filter and the comment claims the endpoint does not support it
findings.body: The previous request sent `environment: selection.environments`, and the removed code is in the diff. The options object at lines 42-53 omits it, with a comment saying the endpoint does not support environment. The endpoint does take the request through `get_snuba_params` (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_trace_item_attributes.py:195) and builds its `SearchResolver` from those params (lines 219-222), so environment appears to be part of the query. The key list may therefore no longer be scoped to the selected environments. Either send `environment` again or confirm the endpoint ignores it and correct the comment. The RPC filtering step was not read, so this rests on the resolver construction.

findings.title: Tooltip and remove-button label still describe overlays that no longer exist
findings.body: Each visualize is now one series and one chart (static/app/views/explore/charts/index.tsx:182-239 maps each visualize to its own chart). The tooltip at line 67 still says the user can "overlay a series onto an existing chart", and the remove button's aria-label at line 194 is "Remove Overlay". Update the copy and label to describe removing a chart.

findings.title: Custom cell renderers that return a falsy value fall back to the default renderer
findings.body: `if (cell)` (lines 31-32 for headers and 70-71 for bodies) treats `0`, `''`, `false` and `null` as "not handled". A custom renderer that returns a valid falsy node is therefore replaced by the default renderer. The JSDoc in tableWidgetVisualization.tsx:37-43 and 50-55, and the story text, say the fallback runs only for `undefined`. Compare with `cell !== undefined` if the documented contract is intended.

findings.title: Multi-yAxis visualize groups now split into one chart per series: is that intended?
findings.body: Before this change, a visualize group with several yAxes rendered one chart with overlays. `getVisualizesFromLocation` (lines 98-108) and `Visualize.fromJSON` (lines 78-82) now produce one Visualize per yAxis. `updateLocationWithAggregateFields` (aggregateFields.tsx:114-120) then rewrites the URL in the split form. Old links and saved queries with multi-yAxis groups will open as several charts with new labels. Is that migration intended, and do saved queries or dashboards that depend on the grouped form need handling?

findings.title: Autofix default changed from 'low' to 'off' in a PR described as replay bulk delete
findings.body: The tests now pin the project default for sentry:autofix_automation_tuning to "off" (test_project.py:812-814; test_project_details.py:2068 and 2076). The diff shows these lines previously expected "low". The default is registered in src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:205, which is in another part of this PR. Projects that never set the option now read "off", and src/sentry/seer/issue_summary.py:253 reads this option; I did not trace what that value gates. The PR body only describes the replay bulk-delete system. Please confirm the default flip is intended and is called out for release.

findings.title: Test title says 'bar charts' but the case asserts LINE
findings.body: The second it.each at line 24 is titled 'defaults to bar charts for %s', but its body (line 26) asserts ChartType.LINE for avg/p50/p75/... The title is wrong, not the assertion (Visualize defaults non-count/sum aggregates to LINE). Rename the title to 'defaults to line charts for %s' so a future reader is not misled.

findings.title: Number-type test's mock matcher checks a parameter the hook never sends
findings.body: In the 'returns empty array for number type' test the matcher at line 120 checks query.query === 'search-query'. The hook sends the search term as substringMatch (useGetTraceItemAttributeValues.tsx:52-53), never as query, so this mock can never match. The assertion at line 146 (expect(searchQueryMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()) therefore cannot show that no request was sent, since the mock only records calls that match (static/app/__mocks__/api.tsx:178, 258). Matching on substringMatch, as the string test at line 73 does, would make the assertion meaningful.

findings.title: Rewrite drops the only check of the request-body log; was that intended?
findings.body: The old tests asserted logger.info('browser_report_received', extra={'request_body': ...}). The rewrite removed those assertions, and no test in this file patches or checks the logger any more (test_basic at line 66 only checks the metric). The endpoint still logs the full request body at info level (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:93). Confirm that dropping this coverage was intentional, or restore an assertion on the log call.

findings.title: Slow-condition map built the same way as production
findings.body: The new `get_slow_conditions_for_groups(list(...))` calls in `TestGetCondition...` (line 409-412) and `TestGetGroupsToFire.setUp` (line 620) match the production call at src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/delayed_workflow.py:651-652, and the helper returns an entry for every id (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/data_condition_group.py:55-58). No issue found; noted for awareness.

findings.title: Error-context assertions do not pin the error message text
findings.body: `test_get_with_error` (lines 209-210) only checks that the substrings `ZeroDivisionError` and `division by zero` appear somewhere in a log entry. The endpoint builds that entry from nodestore keys `title` and `message` (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:114-117). `title` is written onto event data by src/sentry/event_manager.py:788, but `message` is a group kwarg (src/sentry/event_manager.py:818), and `Event.message` reads `logentry` (src/sentry/eventstore/models.py:104-107). If exception events have no top-level `message`, the entry becomes `'ZeroDivisionError: division by zero: '`, and this test would still pass. Could you assert the exact generated line so the test covers the real output format?

findings.title: Duplicated error-event setup in two new tests
findings.body: `test_get_with_error` (141-214) and `test_get_with_error_context_disabled` (216-280) repeat the same event creation, replay storage, segment save and feature-flag block. A helper that stores the error event and replay, returning the event id, would keep the two tests from drifting apart.

findings.title: Top-events log assertions only check the first bucket
findings.body: `assert [{"count": count}] in data[message]["data"][0]` (line 3184) and `assert [{"count": 10}] in other["data"][0]` (line 3189) test `data[...]["data"][0]`, which is a `[timestamp, attrs]` pair, so membership succeeds only through the attrs element of the first hourly bucket. The series has two buckets and the second is never checked. The sibling span test uses `[{"count": n}] in [attrs for _, attrs in results["data"]]` (test_organization_events_stats.py:1458-1460). Matching that form would check every bucket and read as intended.

findings.title: No PUT test for an owner outside the organization
findings.body: The new PUT owner tests (lines 244-331) cover user, team and clear, but not an owner from another organization. The POST counterpart exists (tests/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/test_organization_detector_index.py:525-542). PUT goes through the same ActorField/parse_and_validate_actor path (src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py:37, src/sentry/types/actor.py:293-300), so the risk is low, but the update branch at validators/base/detector.py:66-79 is untested for this input.

contracts.before_after: Before: the summary input contained only breadcrumb log lines for the page. After: it also contains error lines from the full replay error list, computed per page.
contracts.visible_effect: The AI summary for a page can contain errors that belong to other pages, repeated across pages.
contracts.failure_mode: Duplicate or misplaced error lines in the summary; the cause is that error_idx restarts per page.

contracts.before_after: Before: no error lookup. After: one Snuba query and one nodestore read per request, before pagination.
contracts.visible_effect: Each page load adds a whole-replay query. Errors are added to summaries.
contracts.failure_mode: fetch_error_details catches any exception, reports it to Sentry, and returns [] (lines 121-123), so summaries silently lose error context.

contracts.action: Bulk delete: delete recording blobs for matched replays
contracts.before_after: Before and after: rows are archived after recording deletion. The deletion errors are not observed.
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees success while recordings may still exist.
contracts.failure_mode: pool.map results are never iterated, so non-NotFound storage errors are lost (lines 75, 80-83).

contracts.before_after: Before: each report was built with BrowserReport(**report) and counted, with no type or URL validation. After: each report passes BrowserReportSerializer; the first failure returns 422 for the whole batch.

contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:204-205 (same register call, previous value low); src/sentry/constants.py:723-724 (org default)

contracts.before_after: Before: a dash-prefixed line with the title, culprit subtitle and View Issue link (GitHub), and the GitLab equivalent. After: a star-prefixed line with the title as the link, the title truncated to 50 characters, and the environment looked up per issue.

contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/api/base.py:646 (ReleaseAnalyticsMixin records with a guarded user_id); this endpoint passes request.user.id unguarded

summary:
**Batch 1 of 4.** The PR body says only "Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System", but the diff also changes grouping, dashboards, explore, codecov, workflow engine, webhooks, and devservices. I did not confirm the body's claim beyond the storage-error issue in the bulk-delete path. Most significant findings: (1) the replay summary repeats or misplaces errors across pages; (2) the bulk-delete path silently drops non-NotFound storage errors while archiving the replay; (3) the dashboard table flag branch renders empty data. Also flagged: the removed per-variant "Type" row, the autofix default change to "off", and the browser-report batch rejection. Not opened beyond their diffs: the migrations (0917/0920, no-op rewrites pointing at the existing 0921), options/defaults.py, the GitHub and GitLab integration files beyond the cited lines, the codecov, Flex, and button style files, and the other frontend files whose changes are layout or analytics only. I also did not read the full paginate helper, the rest of the replay endpoint, or OwnerModel. Nothing was built or run.

**Batch 1 of 4, retry.** Read all 25 files in this part and the code that decides their effect. One fix-level finding: the autofix tuning default changes from low to off, which silently stops automatic autofix for every project that never saved the option (projectoptions/defaults.py:205; project_option.py:111-114; seer/issue_summary.py:253-254). Three consider-level questions: the merged-PR comment output changed beyond the culprit removal (github/integration.py:404), the assemble analytics fires on every poll and before the feature gate (preprod endpoint:81), and the DB-injection noise config suppresses the first four detections per fingerprint (grouptype.py:514). Also consider: dead format_comment_subtitle helpers, a likely event-attachment ellipsis regression (not rendered), and an unverifiable devservices mode. The PR body describes a replays bulk-delete feature, but this part also changes autofix defaults, grouping noise, PR comment output, Codecov UI and devservices; the author should confirm that scope. Nothing was built or run. options/defaults.py, constants.py and projectoptions/defaults.py were read in their changed regions and their consumers, not in full.

**Batch 2 of 4.** Reviewed all 32 files in part 2. Found 8 items: 3 fix-level regressions, 1 fix-level environment-scoping question, and 4 consider-level items (one a question about intent).

The strongest issues are:
- `attributes.tsx:65`: the hidden-attributes list only applies once a search is typed.
- `traceTabsAndVitals.tsx:93`: the refactor dropped the centering and gap, which changes layout.
- `useTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:50`: `retry: false` was lost, so failing requests keep loading through retries.
- `useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:50`: environment is no longer sent, and the comment claims the endpoint does not support it. The server does build its resolver from environment, so this is probably a regression.

Checked and not flagged: the `Visualize` refactor's callers (`useSaveQuery`, `exploreParams`, `explore/utils` saved-query path, `aggregateColumnEditorModal`, `tables/index`) all map correctly, and `charts/index.tsx` still returns `dedupedYAxes`. The feedback list grid change fixes an invalid `minmax(1fr, …)` value.

Notes:
- The PR body is "Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System", but the diff is mainly the Explore visualize refactor and related UI. The description does not cover this part.
- Some files were checked by their diff hunks and call-site searches rather than full reads: `useAnalytics.tsx`, `useExploreTimeseries.tsx`, `spansTab.tsx`, `toolbarSaveAs.tsx`, `traceWaterfall.tsx` (its `height:100%` was dropped), `teamMisery.tsx`, `profileSummary`, `explore/types.tsx`, `useExploreAggregatesTable.tsx`, `useTopEvents.tsx`, `toolbarSortBy.tsx`, and `aggregateColumnEditorModal.tsx`.
- Analytics payloads for `visualizes` changed shape (`label` dropped, `chartType` omitted when not user-selected). I did not check the consumers, so I left it out of findings.
- Nothing was built or run.

**Batch 3 of 4.** Reviewed all 25 files in this part plus the deleted 0917 migration test (diff only; the file no longer exists at head). Most of the change is layout swaps to the Flex component and test rewrites. I checked the expected strings against their sources: the PR-comment newline layout (GitHub and GitLab), browser-reporting serializer error messages, formatPercentage and formatRate outputs, the Visualize class API and toJSON shape, the modal's onColumnsChange output, and the fixture slugs (foo for GitHub, baz for GitLab). The deleted 0917 test is consistent with the migration, which is now a no-op, and 0921 still has its own test. Findings: one question on the autofix default change, which the PR description does not mention, and three test-quality notes (a misnamed test, a mock matcher that can never match, and a dropped log assertion). Two contracts are open: the integration card's flex-basis change, and whether ProjectsStore is loaded on every path into the replay AI tab. Limits: I read test_project_details.py and test_project.py only around the changed lines, not in full. I did not run any tests or builds.

**Batch 4 of 4.** Reviewed the five test files in part 4. No blockers or fixes. The owner tests for detector create/update match the validator and serializer, the delayed-workflow test passes the same slow-condition map that production builds, and the replay error-context tests match the endpoint. Findings are test-quality items: the logs top-events assertions check only the first hourly bucket, the replay error assertions are substring checks that do not pin the message text, the replay tests duplicate setup, and the PUT owner tests lack an out-of-organization case. One open question is whether exception events carry a top-level `message` in nodestore; this affects the replay error line in production and is outside this part's files.
